description.narrative: International Alert is an independent peacebuilding non-governmental organisation with a global mission to work with people in conflict-affected and -threatened areas to make a positive difference for peace; to improve the substance and implementation of international policies relevant to peacebuilding; and to strengthen the peacebuilding sector, with a key focus on gender, prevention of violent extremism and economic development for peace. Its main methods of engagement include bringing people together through dialogue; capacity building through trainings, accompaniment (which involves offering continuous guidance and advice to people, organisations and companies as they build peace or operate in high-risk places) and undertaking policy research and advocacy. With Headquarters in London, United Kingdom, Alert is active in 27 countries and territories across all continents.

International Alert är en oberoende och icke-statlig organisation med globalt fredsbyggande uppdrag att arbeta med människor i konflikt-drabbade och -hotade områden för att ha en positiv inverkan för fred, att stärka grunden och implementeringen av internationella policies som är relevanta för fredsbyggande, och att stärka den fredsbyggande sektor, med ett tydligt fokus på jämställdhet, förebyggande av våldsam extremism och ekonomisk utveckling för fred. Dess huvudsakliga arbetssätt är att föra människor samman via dialog, kapacitetsutveckling via utbildningar, medföljande (vilket innebär att ge löpande vägledning och råd till människor, organisationer och företag när de bygger fred eller verkar i högriskområden) och att genomföra policyforskning och påverkansarbete. Alert har huvudkontor i London, Storbritannien och är aktiv i 27 länder och områden över alla kontinenter.

The overall objectives of the intervention are shown below. This is the mission statement of International Alert, which informs the Strategic Perspective 2015-2019 and which will guide the new strategy from 2020. The overall objectives are: 1.) to work with people in conflict-affected and -threatened areas to make a positive difference for peace 2.) to improve the substance and implementation of international policies relevant to peacebuilding 3.) to strengthen the peacebuilding sector. Based on this, the Strategic Perspective outlines six Pathways: Relations within and between communities (1); State-Citizen Relations (2); Gender relations (3); Crime, violence and instability (CVI) (4); Natural Resource Management and Climate Change (5); and Economic development for peace (6). Each pathway has a specific set of expected results, which guides all work of Alert. A country or regional programme may contribute to one or several of the pathways.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
[Please note that this text is mainly based on Sida's latest assessment of reporting from International Alert.]
The consequences of Covid-10, the shrinking of civic space and funding cuts has been a challenge to implementation in many countries. However, Alert managed during the grant period to move forward and maintain peacebuilding space in a number of fragile contexts. Dialogue and conflict prevention at the community level remains core business for International Alert, while the organisation keeps pushing formore efective peacebuilding strategies at the global level.
As of 2021, Alert collaborates with 132 partners around the world with whom they engaged with and supported 98,440 people. 54% of these were women, 45% were men and 1% identified as other or preferred not to reveal their gender identity. 162 advocacy and influencing initiatives were undertaken directly reaching 20,292 individuals. Alert continued to work with in partnerships with capacity strengthening and mentoring, including of local and international organisations in the aid sector, individuals and governments; 2021 involved 17,034 individuals (54% women, 43% men, 3% other) as part of these activities. Dialogue remains core business to Alert, and the final report includes numerous examples. Altogether, Alert and its partners facilitated 758 dialogue meetings, bringing together a total of 46,993 people (54% women, 45,5% men, 0,5% other) to talk. Specific and thematic achievements of particular interest to the Swedish Strategy for Sustainable Peace 2017-2022 includes the areas Youth Peace and Security; Women Peace and Security, Conflict sensitivity; and environment/ climate related conflicts. A few examples of this work is described here:
During the grant period, Alert has expanded it's work on conflict sensitivity and conflict analysis. 2021 saw the establishment of a Conflict Hub in Democratic Republic of Congo. The hum is focused solely on providing conflict sensitivity and conflict analysis expertise to organisations working in the development and humanitarian field, and promoting conflict sensitive investments in the private sector in the region. With regards to Women Peace and Security including work on masculinities, Alert has worked to strengthen women's meaningful participation and inclusion, for example in Kenya, where Alert has facilitated consultations with the Council of Elders to endorse two women as local political candidates for the first time in 2021. Alert has also worked with advocacy and research on gender issues around perceptions of masculinity, gender norms and sexual and gender minorities in Kyrgyzstan, Nepal, the Philippines and Nigeria. Furthermore, Alert has supported cross-border traders in DRC, Rwanda and Burundi, who often face harassment, illustrates how our five peace factors come together. Two-thirds of these traders are women, for whom the trade provides a meagre but essential income. International Alert has worked with them to better protect their rights and hold customs officials to account, supporting the development and organisation of small trader cooperatives and teaching negotiation techniques, tax classification and small business management. Border officials have been trained to re-shape their interactions with cross-border traders and state officials and traders have been brought together to voice and address grievances and tackle obstacles to trade. These efforts have resulted in 60% fewer cases of harassment like physical or verbal abuse and extortion at the border, helping boost incomes while improving relations between cross-border communities, the state and citizens. With regards to Youth Peace and Security, Alert has mobilised youths, for example in Rwanda, to act as local peace messengers, to improve trust and collaboration between families of genocide perpetrators and survivors. In Lebanon, Alert brought together local authorities and young people to undertake an analysis of the conflict dynamics in central Bekaa, an area which hosts a large concentration of Syrian refugees. Open discussions were held and joint community initiatives planned through the youth group. In South Caucasus - Georgia/ Abkhazia, Alert has worked to empower youth leaders to shape and influence public debate through local campaigns on issues like violence against women and inclusion of minority rights. Alert has made efforts to scale up work on Natural Resource Management and Climate related to conflict. Mali is one example of this work, where disputes between farming, herding and fishing communities over access to land and water is a major driver of conflict. International Alert has developed a strategic plan to more systematically integrate natural resource management as a pathway to peace through engagement with conflict-affected communities. Focus has been on engaging groups that are traditionally excluded from decision making (such as women and youth).
